summary: Defines a registry for profile URIs to be used in specifications that standardize profiles.

plainLanguage.summary: A profile URI identifies extra rules or conventions for a data format. RFC 7284 sets up an IANA registry so specifications can record profile URIs and explain what they mean.

questions: how do i register a profile uri
subtitle: A public registry for profile URIs used by specifications.

tldr.problem: Profiles can be identified without central coordination, but independently created profile URIs can make interoperability and coordination harder.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC establishes an IANA registry with a documented registration template and a First Come First Served policy.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7284 is informational and defines the Profile URIs registry for specifications that standardize profiles.

today: RFC 7284 is informational. It defines an IANA registry for profile URIs used in specifications that standardize profiles.

sections.title: Why Register Profile URIs
sections.content:
A profile can signal extra semantics, such as constraints, conventions, or extensions, without changing the basic semantics of a media type. A profile is identified by a URI, so profiles can be created without central coordination.

The RFC establishes an IANA registry to help support interoperability and reduce coupling between clients and servers. The two sides can rely on a shared profile contract rather than being designed specifically for each other.
sections.plainLanguage: A profile URI names extra rules for interpreting a format. A shared registry helps different systems identify and use the same documented profile.

sections.title: Registration Requirements
sections.content:
A registration requires a URI whose meaning is described in a permanent, readily available public specification. The description must provide enough detail for independent implementations to interoperate.

The registration form includes the profile URI, a common name, a short description, and a reference to the specification. The reference is recommended but may be omitted if the description itself is sufficient. Notes are optional. The RFC gives an example request using a fictional URI.
sections.plainLanguage: To register a profile, provide its URI, name, and description. The meaning must be documented clearly enough for separate implementations to work together.

sections.title: Registry Policy and Initial Entries
sections.content:
The registration policy is First Come First Served. The initial registry lists five entries: an example profile URI, a Dublin Core HTML metadata profile, and three JSON-LD profiles named expanded, compacted, and flattened.

The RFC says there are no additional security considerations beyond those inherent in using URIs, and points to RFC 3986 for general URI security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry starts with five profile URIs and accepts registrations on a First Come First Served basis. The RFC adds no security concerns beyond those of URIs generally.
